overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance heavily favors space-based 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary anomaly hooks. Videos structured around hypothetical extreme environment survival (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, burning ice worlds) consistently drive higher initial velocity, views-per-day, and engagement (likes-per-view) compared to general psychological tricks or older standard static facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Extreme Environment 'What If' Space Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed standard descriptive space facts posted in the same window.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersive space survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme, high-value planetary phenomena.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Planetary Extremes & Rare Cosmic Anomalies
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) generated strong organic discovery and high like ratios within the first week.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing on exotic exoplanets with extreme physical properties (weird weather, absolute darkness, extreme pressure) paired with punchy, high-curiosity titles.

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Velocity Psychological Tricks & Static Science Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) showed very low velocity and minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological life-hacks and standard trivia unless reframed into high-stakes narrative framing.

next_video.hook_style: What if scenario with extreme physical stakes
next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Place in the Universe (The Boomerang Nebula)?
next_video.opening_direction: Instantly drop the viewer into absolute zero temperatures where atoms freeze stiffer than steel in milliseconds.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this cosmic frost pocket is actually colder than the background radiation of deep space itself, freezing light in its tracks.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary/cosmic survival format while introducing a fresh, untouched astronomical phenomenon (The Boomerang Nebula).
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not use diamonds, burning ice, glass rain, or dark planets
Must feature absolute zero physics and nebula survival mechanics
